body: Forward test of the promise-tracker credibility method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.60 (naive base rate 0.55) that: Bajaj Finance consolidated AUM growth YoY at 31-Mar-2027 is ≥26.0%. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (19-Oct-2026): AUM +26.5% YoY to ₹5,84,624 cr; net AUM add ~₹38k cr/qtr for two quarters. CEO Rajeev Jain: 'probably between 26%, 27% growth we should deliver now on a full year basis'; medium-term guide stays 20–25%. Headwinds named: RBI hikes ('baking in two more increases… 6% kind of rates'), NIM compression slightly worse than the 10–15 bps guide, gold-loan short-tenor schemes stopped, El Niño (monsoon 87% LPA). Track record: FY25 guide 26–27%, delivered ~26%. Reasoning: BFL has a long record of hitting AUM guidance, and the guide was given with H1 already at 26.5%; but 26% is the bottom of the range and rate hikes plus rural stress lean against H2 acceleration. Slightly above base. Resolution: YES if consolidated AUM at 31-Mar-2027 ÷ consolidated AUM at 31-Mar-2026 − 1 ≥ 26.0% (both as stated in BFL's Q4 FY27 results press release/investor deck; use BFL's own reported YoY if it states one). Source: Bajaj Finance Q4 FY27 results press release / investor presentation (NSE announcements). Resolve by 2027-05-15; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: A large lender restating a full-year growth range at H1 with H1 at/above the range bottom meets the range bottom roughly 55% of the time (range bottoms are often missed by tenths).
data.resolution_rule: YES if consolidated AUM at 31-Mar-2027 ÷ consolidated AUM at 31-Mar-2026 − 1 ≥ 26.0% (both as stated in BFL's Q4 FY27 results press release/investor deck; use BFL's own reported YoY if it states one).

title: Paper call: Bajaj Finance consolidated AUM growth YoY at 31-Mar-2027 is ≥26.0%
